# CC0 / Public-Domain Art Reference Kit  
## Fantasy Items & Equipment

A curated, quality-first set of CC0 and public-domain resources for drawing and designing fantasy-game items: weapons, armor, adventuring gear, potions, magic objects, containers, and environmental props.

---

## How to use this kit

1. **Use historical armor and weapons** to establish believable construction, materials, weight, and wear.
2. **Use game-asset collections** to study readable silhouettes, icon design, and fantasy exaggeration.
3. **Use 3D models** to rotate objects, understand form, and test lighting.
4. **Use Poly Haven** for realistic materials, HDRIs, and render support.
5. **Design in tiers**: mundane equipment, crafted equipment, enchanted equipment, and legendary artifacts.

---

## Weapons and armor

| Resource | Best for | License / status |
|---|---|---|
| [Rawpixel — Armor images](https://www.rawpixel.com/search/armor) | Museum-quality armor references: field armor, tournament armor, helmets, gauntlets, knightly equipment, and historical construction details. | Public Domain / CC0 where labeled |
| [Rawpixel — Public-domain medieval weapons](https://www.rawpixel.com/search/medieval%20weapons) | Swords, polearms, shields, and period weapon illustrations; useful for silhouette and ornament studies. | Public Domain / CC0 where labeled |
| [OpenGameArt — CC0 Weapons collection](https://opengameart.org/content/cc0-weapons-0) | Large curated CC0 set: swords, axes, hammers, shields, spears, bows, daggers, helmets, and some modern/sci-fi weapons. | CC0 on tagged assets |
| [OpenGameArt — CC0 3D Weapons](https://opengameart.org/content/cc0-3d-weapons) | 3D weapons and related models, including fantasy swords, bows, daggers, cannons, and RPG item models. | CC0 on tagged assets |

**Primary use:** Rawpixel is strongest for realistic historical reference; OpenGameArt is strongest for stylized game-ready forms and fantasy variation.

## Magic, treasure, and adventuring gear

- **Potions and alchemy:** Look for potion bottles, ingredient jars, flasks, herbs, scrolls, and crafting stations in OpenGameArt’s item and prop collections.  
  <https://opengameart.org/content/cc0-items>

- **Treasure and currency:** Use chests, coin piles, gems, jewelry, keys, maps, and relics to establish reward language in a fantasy setting.  
  <https://opengameart.org/content/items-5>

- **Camping and travel gear:** Study tents, bedrolls, lanterns, torches, ropes, canteens, backpacks, cooking pots, and tools. These make characters and environments feel lived-in.

- **Books, scrolls, and arcane items:** Use runes, crystals, spellbooks, wands, staves, and ritual props for magic-system visual identity.  
  <https://opengameart.org/content/props>

| [OpenGameArt — CC0 3D Weapons](https://opengameart.org/content/cc0-3d-weapons) | Turning weapons in space and studying proportions, grips, and construction. | CC0 on tagged assets |
| [Poly Haven](https://polyhaven.com/) | CC0 HDRIs, textures, materials, and 3D assets for lighting and rendering studies. | CC0 |

Poly Haven is especially useful for metal, leather, wood, cloth, stone, and glass materials—the core surface families in fantasy equipment design.

## Design framework

### Equipment tiers

| Tier | Purpose | Visual language |
|---|---|---|
| Mundane | Everyday function | Simple shapes, practical materials, visible wear |
| Crafted | Professional quality | Cleaner construction, better materials, regional detail |
| Enchanted | Magical function | Glow, runes, unusual materials, impossible details |
| Legendary | Story and status | Strong silhouette, ornament, material contrast, narrative damage or history |

### Item-design checklist

- **Silhouette:** Can the item be identified from a distance?
- **Function:** Does its shape suggest how it is held, worn, or used?
- **Material story:** Does metal, leather, wood, bone, cloth, or crystal communicate origin and value?
- **Wear:** Are there scratches, dents, repairs, dirt, patina, or broken parts?
- **Fantasy logic:** Does the magical element enhance the object rather than obscure its function?
- **Scale:** Does it read correctly beside a hand, body, backpack, or creature?

## Recommended starter set

1. **Rawpixel armor and medieval weapons** — historical realism and construction  
2. **OpenGameArt CC0 Weapons** — broad stylized weapon range  
3. **OpenGameArt Generic Fantasy RPG Items** — inventory and icon design  
4. **OpenGameArt RPG Item Collection 1** — rotatable 3D item forms  
5. **Poly Haven** — materials, lighting, and render support  

---

## License notes

- **CC0** means “no rights reserved.” You may use, modify, redistribute, and commercialize assets without attribution, though credit is courteous.
- **Rawpixel’s Public Domain License** states that images labeled “Free Public Domain CC0 Image” are available under CC0 for personal and commercial use without attribution. [web:42]
- **OpenGameArt collections** can mix licenses. Confirm the license shown on each individual asset page before downloading or redistributing.
- For production work, keep a local license log with the asset name, source URL, license, author, and download date.
